items.title: Carmen Lundy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 15, 2023
items.q: I know that Joni Mitchell for example writes the other way, she writes her lyrics and then sets the music to that.

ctx.x: Yeah, can you recall if the phrase or the upward four note melodic line came first?

I believe that the melodic — I tend to write the music first. I might have an idea of what’s coming lyrically but I generally write tunes and then, because I find the lyric to be the most challenging aspect of songwriting or composition, that the lyric has to be undoubtedly the hardest part. I know that Joni Mitchell for example writes the other way, she writes her lyrics and then sets the music to that. That tune, I’ve always loved the cello. I’m a mezzo, the cello is in the range of my voice. I’ve always loved…

I got this idea, the perfect fifths going on, and I’m thinking how can I convey to the listener this vulnerable place that we all live in as human beings, wanting and aspiring to the same things. Love, fulfillment, vocation, employment, stability, homeownership, whatever the heck. We all aspire to these things as humans. So I was like how can I take this idea I had — that’s when I started singing [sings arpeggio] in perfect fourths, the interval the fourth. So now I’ve got this fifth thing going on with the…
